legend: Anteroposterior radiograph of the humerus demonstrates features of an aggressive chondrosarcoma. In addition to the proximal region with ring-and-arc mineralizations, the distal region demonstrates prominent lytic features with cortical destruction.

Sagittal T2-weighted fat-suppressed MRI demonstrates features of an aggressive chondrosarcoma. While the proximal region shows a lobulated mass of high signal and punctated signal voids consistent with chondroid matrix and calcifications, the distal region demonstrates a more homogeneous intermediate signal reflecting higher cellularity. Note also the deep cortical scalloping and high signal intensity of periosteal reaction distally.

Resection specimen of the dedifferentiated chondrosarcoma corresponding to the radiograph and MRI shown. The proximal region shows areas of blue to greyish cartilage, associated with a fleshy tan area distally.
The tumour is characterized by an admixture of both a low-grade cartilaginous component and a high-grade non-cartilaginous sarcoma component, with an abrupt transition.
This tumour demonstrates prominent heterologous osteosarcomatous differentiation, with scant associated low-grade cartilaginous component (upper right).

This rare example shows heterologous squamous differentiation with overt keratinization (upper left). The tumour was diffusely immunoreactive for cytokeratins and p40/p63 in the dedifferentiated component (not shown).
This tumour displays predominantly nondescript high-grade spindle cell morphology, with scant associated low-grade cartilaginous component (lower right).

Dedifferentiated chondrosarcoma is present as an undifferentiated spindle cell sarcoma component adjacent to a low-grade cartilaginous comoponent within the medullary cavity. The dedifferentiated component invades the cortex and extends into soft tissue with an associated periosteal reaction.
High-grade sarcoma arising in association with a low-grade cartilaginous neoplasm.
